reasons: Degenerate metric: best candidate has only 3 trades across 384 sessions. A Sharpe ratio estimated from 3 trades is not a reliable statistic and is highly susceptible to noise.

Degenerate metric: best candidate has only 1 downside session. The Sortino ratio denominator is near-zero (downside volatility estimated from 1 session), making the fallback to Sharpe appropriate but the resulting Sharpe itself unreliable with only 3 trades.

Extreme kurtosis (126.04) and high skew (2.20) in the best candidate indicate the return distribution is heavily non-normal, dominated by outlier events. With only 3 trades, these moments are estimated from almost nothing.
Net PnL of 0.63 on 3 trades means the result rests on a handful of sessions. The strategy's performance is not diversified across independent observations.

Gate p-value of 0.824 is far above any reasonable significance threshold, and the observed best score (0.0256) is well below the null mean (0.0608) and far below the 5th percentile of the null distribution (0.0980). The result is indistinguishable from noise.
auditors.confidence_note: I cannot see the strategy code or how these 3 trades were selected, but the statistical foundation is too thin: a ratio estimated from 3 independent observations with extreme higher moments is not a reliable basis for any claim.

reasons: The hypothesis asks 'does an outsized move continue or give it back?' — a question requiring directional consistency across the ordinary run of sessions. The strategy traded in only 3 of 384 sessions (0.78%). This is a degenerate optimum: the strategy maximised its score by trading almost never, not by finding an edge. The hypothesis explicitly states 'A story that only works on the largest handful of moves in the sample is a story about a handful of moves. What would be worth knowing is whether the effect is there across the ordinary run of sessions, in one direction' — this result violates that requirement.

Commission paid ($0.06) is 8.7% of gross P&L ($0.69). On 3 trades, this is $0.02 per trade in commission against $0.23 gross per trade. The net result ($0.63) is driven entirely by the cost structure of inactivity, not by a replicable signal. The strategy found that not trading scores well when trading is costly.

The Sharpe per session of 0.0256 with only 3 sessions of exposure means the metric is measuring noise across 384 sessions, 381 of which had zero activity. This is not a meaningful economic result — it is an artifact of extreme selectivity combined with a cost structure that rewards inactivity.
auditors.confidence_note: I cannot see the fill model details or whether the entry/exit logic correctly implements the two-bar fade pattern as written, but the trade count and session coverage are sufficient to veto on economic grounds independent of those details.

reasons: Extreme concentration: best_session_share of 0.5 means a single session accounts for 50% of total profit. Removing it would flip the result from positive to negative.
Minimal trade count: only 3 trades executed across 384 sessions. The strategy is almost entirely inactive, making any observed profit unreliable.
Profit concentration in top 5%: 100% of profits come from the top 5% of sessions, indicating the result is entirely dependent on a handful of outlier outcomes.

Temporal clustering: positive returns concentrated in exactly two months (Nov and Dec 2024) and two specific hours (09 and 18 UTC), with a single negative month (Aug). This is a narrow temporal window.
Only 1 downside session across 3 sessions with exposure suggests insufficient negative outcome sampling to assess robustness.

Tiny per-cell counts acknowledged by the campaign itself ('at a few hundred sessions the per-cell counts in these breakdowns are tiny'), making the by_hour and by_weekday breakdowns unreliable for assessing true patterns.
auditors.confidence_note: The data clearly shows extreme concentration in both time and outcome space; the robustness axis is the one place where this concentration is directly visible and measurable.
